Every code panel is a verbatim excerpt of godot/ at c3e12737d9b38679efa61622cb62c793935aff59; every gameplay shot is a real Movie Maker capture of an isolated copy of that revision, driven through the real input map by the disclosed capture driver; fixture strips and play-check shots are labelled as such. beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer; reconstructed Walker prompt from Bao's CHANGE-BRIEF.md (not a recorded session). Liam introduces himself.
beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Bear. Bao Xing's particle assignment: add two effects to a Godot game that already works, tune each one from what you actually see, test it, read the shader Godot generates, and price it on the CPU and the GPU. The game is Lanternfall again. Here is the ask, rebuilt from Bao's change brief.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about particle effects for Lanternfall, warm sparks on every weapon hit and a short ember trail behind the courier, into Godot 4 CPUParticles2D scenes. beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer. The framing a viewer arrives with ('particles are decoration') is corrected to what the film shows ('particles are feedback').
beats.narration_text: The short version. These particles are feedback, not decoration. Each one answers a real event in the game: a hit, a step, a new level. And none of them is allowed to change a single rule. That contract is what the rest of this film checks.

props.title: One burst per hit.
props.source: godot/effects/particle_presentation.gd · lines 47–57 · source revision c3e1273 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _on_weapon_hit(at: Vector2) -> void:
	hits_seen += 1
	if session.state.current != GS.PLAYING or hit_bursts.size() >= MAX_HIT_BURSTS:
		return
	var burst := HitScene.instantiate() as CPUParticles2D
	add_child(burst)
	burst.global_position = session.to_global(at)
	hit_bursts.append(burst)
	burst.finished.connect(_on_hit_finished.bind(burst))
	burst.restart()
	hits_spawned += 1

beats.narration_text: Effect B, the trail, is decided once per physics frame. Line one twenty-six measures how far the courier actually moved since the last frame. Holding a key isn't enough. props.title: A trail that needs real movement.
props.source: godot/effects/particle_presentation.gd · lines 121–131 · source revision c3e1273 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if not is_instance_valid(session) or not is_instance_valid(trail):
		return
	_apply_policy()
	var current: Vector2 = session.player.global_position
	var distance: float = current.distance_to(previous_position) if have_position else 0.0
	var teleport_limit: float = session.player.speed * delta * 2.0 + 4.0
	trail.global_position = current + Vector2(0, 7)
	trail.emitting = session.state.current == GS.PLAYING and trail.is_visible_in_tree() and distance > 0.01 and distance <= teleport_limit
	previous_position = current
	have_position = true
output: reads session.player and session.state; writes only the trail

func _on_leveled_up(_level: int) -> void:
	levels_seen += 1
	if session.state.current != GS.PLAYING or level_bursts.size() >= MAX_LEVEL_BURSTS:
		return
	var burst := LevelScene.instantiate() as CPUParticles2D
	_sync_overlay()
	level_overlay.add_child(burst)
	burst.position = session.hud.levelup_particle_anchor()
	level_bursts.append(burst)
	burst.finished.connect(_on_level_finished.bind(burst))
	burst.restart()

beats.narration_text: One policy runs every frame, and it only reads the game. When the game isn't playing, hit bursts and the trail get a speed scale of zero, so they freeze exactly where they are. beats.role_note: Code beat (code-then-result-v1): shaders/particles_generated.gdshader lines 340-352 at c3e1273, read verbatim; the next beat shows the result.
beats.narration_text: Under the hood. Godot turned a GPU copy of the burst into this generated process shader. Every frame, for every spark, it adds up the velocity, moves the spark, and then samples the colour ramp and the scale curve by the spark's age, on line three forty-seven. In Bao's words, this is the process stage: how a particle changes. Drawing it is a separate stage.

beats.role_note: Result of B22. Recorded measurements (evidence/assignment-6/cost/*.json) drawn as bars; nothing estimated.
beats.narration_text: The measured price. On the CPU, thirty-two live bursts add about nine thousandths of a millisecond a frame, a tenth at the spawn spike, and the trail four thousandths, all far under budget. The GPU number is the honest part: under the game's renderer, this Mac reports zero on every frame. A Vulkan proxy can measure it, and the difference stays inside the noise.

beats.role_note: ClaudeVerdictArtifact — implemented work, limitations, human judgment; shows the source revision.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Implemented: three effects that answer real events and never write game state, with two hundred ninety-two checks behind them.
